title: PaceStreak app — home screen structure
question: The brand world is settled (near-black, lime, flame, the five-level grid). This picks how the home screen and log flow are composed. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: The Ledger
options.thesis: Home is your training log itself: a running ledger of days, with the streak as its masthead.
options.viewport: Masthead: streak weeks huge, this week's 7 day-ticks under it. Below, today's row open for a one-tap log; past days scroll as dated ledger lines, rest days quietly marked 'rest · kept'.
options.risk: The year grid moves off home; the 'watch it fill' moment lives one tap away on Progress.

options.label: The Grid
options.thesis: Home is the year: the activity grid fills the first screen and the streak lives inside it.
options.viewport: A full-width 26-week grid with kept weeks banded in lime; streak count overlaid top-left; a large Log button docked at thumb height opens a bottom sheet.
options.risk: Beautiful at month six, empty and discouraging on day one — needs a strong first-run state.

options.label: The Week
options.thesis: Home is this week, because the week is the unit: seven day slots against your target, filled by tapping.
options.viewport: Seven vertical day slots fill the screen; tapping today's slot logs; the target is a line across the slots you fill toward. Streak and freezes sit above, chains swipe sideways.
options.risk: Long-term progress (grid, records) is secondary; strong for habit, weaker for 'watch it compound'.
